sections.heading: Operating-point gain variation
sections.text: The small-signal control-to-output gain of a buck-boost varies strongly with duty cycle. If the input range is wide, design the voltage-loop gain at the worst-case operating point (maximum duty, minimum input) and verify margin at the boost extreme rather than the buck extreme.

sections.heading: Right-half-plane zero
sections.text: In CCM boost-mode operation, a buck-boost exhibits a right-half-plane zero whose frequency scales with load current and (1 - D)^2. Place the voltage-loop crossover at least a factor of 3 below the worst-case RHPZ frequency; chasing higher bandwidth produces non-minimum-phase undershoot that no inner current loop can hide.

sections.heading: Inner current loop bandwidth
sections.text: Set the inner current-loop crossover roughly fsw/10 in CCM. In DCM the small-signal current dynamics collapse to a single pole and the current loop can be made much faster, but verify the mode boundary explicitly — switching between CCM and DCM mid-transient is a frequent source of evaluation failures.

sections.heading: Sign convention
sections.text: Inverting buck-boost topologies require careful sign tracking in both sensor scaling and controller output. A polarity error here is indistinguishable in early simulation from an under-tuned controller — verify open-loop step response polarity before tightening gains.
